check: verify that Test-S5Stress.ps1 correctly rejects a failed profile, using the preserved failed report as a fixture
why: The script is the tool that will read the 24-hour verdict. If it judged by exit code alone it would accept anything, since StressFixture halts with server.halt(false) and a failed profile still exits 0. That exact defect was found earlier in this session, so the repaired version deserves testing against a real failure rather than a reading.

fixtureUsed.failure: java.util.concurrent.CancellationException: stress stop timed out waiting for in-flight chunks

result: The script computes reportPassed as false and therefore passed as false regardless of exit code, so it rejects the failed profile. The preserved failure is usable as a regression fixture.

anApparentGapThatIsNotOne.observation: reportDurationMet is computed at line 108 and recorded at line 120 but never appears in the pass decision at line 109, which looks like an unchecked condition.
anApparentGapThatIsNotOne.whyItIsFine: StressFixture line 179 defines passed as failure being null, completed chunks exceeding zero, checkpoints being non-empty, and durationMet - so durationMet is already inside the field the script reads. The script cannot accept a run that failed the duration check.
anApparentGapThatIsNotOne.endToEnd: scriptPassed true implies report.passed true implies durationMet true, necessarily. And when durationMet is false the fixture records a failure note and sets passed false, which the script rejects.
anApparentGapThatIsNotOne.whyItIsRecordedAnyway: Keeping reportDurationMet in execution.json makes the reasoning auditable - a reader can see the duration condition was considered rather than having to infer it from the fixture's source.

theExitCodeNoteIsInTheScript: execution.json carries an exitCodeIsNotAVerdict field stating that StressFixture halts with server.halt(false) so a failed profile still exits 0, and that the report is what decides. That is the defect documented where the next reader will see it.
